svg.title: A client who requires assistance with bathing tells the nurse they feel humiliated at needing help. Which action best supports the client's dignity?
svg.desc: Loss of control is the source of the distress, so returning choices and letting the client do any part of the care directly addresses it. Telling the client not to feel embarrassed dismisses the feeling rather than resolving it, and adding staff increases exposure instead of reducing it.

g.text: STUDY HUB / QUESTION MAP
Dignity in Hygiene
Read the situation
A client who requires assistance with
bathing tells the nurse they feel
humiliated at needing help. Which action
best supports the client's dignity?
What fits here
Let the client wash whatever areas they
can and ask how they prefer the care to be
done
Why it fits
Loss of control is the source of the
distress, so returning choices and letting
the client do any part of the care
directly addresses it. Telling the client
not to feel embarrassed dismisses the
feeling rather than resolving it, and
adding staff increases exposure instead of
reducing it.
